item: The arena cap is the server's alone: the launcher gives it to the server's command, the browser does not inherit it, and the LLM engines the server starts leave the launcher's default out (the coordinator's check of #1304, should-fix 1)
key_paths: scripts/launch.sh; src/llm/model_store.py; src/llm/installer.py; tests/test_malloc_arena_default.py; docs/CHANGES.md; docs/ledger/RULINGS_INDEX.md; docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md; docs/ledger/LESSONS.md
summary: R114 ruled the cap for the instance, and the launcher exported it, so every process the launcher or the server started inherited it: the browser opened by xdg-open, and the Ollama daemon, the vLLM server and the installs and weights download (all built by launch_env from os.environ). Nothing ruled or measured the cap for those, and the diagnostics read only the server's. The launcher now hands the value to the server's command alone through env, so a readonly declaration in oo.env cannot stop the app starting, marks its own default with OO_ARENA_MAX_DEFAULTED=1 (cleared first, so a marker the caller's environment carried is never taken for this launcher's word), and launch_env drops the variable when the marker says it was the launcher's default and always drops the marker; a number the operator chose is unmarked and still reaches the engines. The decision is recorded in the R114 row and queue entry as a session decision under 16c. The Ollama install script (installer.run_installer) is a deliberate non-member of the three spawners (the coordinator's check of the fix): a short shell, not an engine, which inherits the server's environment as it is, the daemon it installs being started by the service manager; the code, launch_env's docstring and the spawner test say so. Tests run the real launcher against fake server, browser and curl on both paths (a fresh start and already running), and the three spawners; fourteen mutations are each caught. Lesson: LESSONS.md, A DEFAULT RULED AND MEASURED FOR ONE PROCESS IS GIVEN TO THAT PROCESS'S COMMAND, NOT EXPORTED TO EVERYTHING IT STARTS.
